Pros:
Original CHT design — patented EP3445568A1 / US11712847B2, precise machining
Nickel coating resists corrosion and plastic adhesion
Widest size range of any CHT nozzle (0.25–1.8mm)
5-pack available at volume discount
Cons:
5× the price of AliExpress clones with identical flow performance
Not abrasive-safe — nickel coating is not hardened
Requires 6mm wrench (standard)
Name: CHT
Description: The original Bondtech CHT (Core Heating Technology) nozzle, manufactured by Bondtech AB under their EP3445568A1 / US11712847B2 patents. The CHT design splits filament into 3 strands via multiple bore holes, increasing heating wall surface area and enabling 25–35% higher volumetric flow vs standard nozzles (CNCKitchen validated). The Bondtech version adds a nickel coating for corrosion resistance and reduced plastic adhesion. Fits standard M6×1×7.5×12.5 RepRap spec heat blocks — compatible with E3D V6, Dragon, Rapido, Mosquito, Copperhead, and all M6 variants. The $5 Mellow/Trianglelab clones deliver the same flow results if budget is a priority.
Verdict Label: The original CHT — patented, precise machining, widest size range

Pros:
German-made by Brozzl GmbH with tight manufacturing tolerances (±0.01mm concentricity ≤0.02mm)
Ruby tip: high hardness, non-stick surface, excellent for abrasive filaments
Inner hole roughness ≤Ra0.4, ruby hole roughness ≤Ra0.012 — precision-machined
V6 (M6) and MK8 threading available
Cons:
Price not listed on site — sold exclusively through European resellers
Harder to source in North America vs. Ruby tips from E3D or other brands
Ruby has lower thermal conductivity than brass — may need temperature adjustment
Name: Ruby
Description: Brozzl GmbH is a German manufacturer of precision 3D printer nozzles. Their Ruby Nozzle combines a brass body with a synthetic ruby gemstone insert at the tip, providing extreme hardness for abrasive filament resistance alongside a naturally smooth, non-stick surface. Manufactured to tighter tolerances than most competitors: ±0.01mm orifice tolerance, concentricity ≤0.02mm, inner hole roughness ≤Ra0.4. Available in V6 (M6) and MK8 threading in multiple diameters. Pricing not listed on website — sold through European resellers. Can be found via 3DJake, Amazon.de, and similar.

Pros:
25–35% flow rate improvement over standard brass at 0.6mm+ (CNCKitchen validated)
~$5 vs $25 for original Bondtech CHT
Standard M6 thread — fits any V6-compatible block
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe (brass wears quickly with CF/GF)
Quality varies by vendor batch
Clone status — no official documentation
Name: CHT Brass
Description: Third-party implementation of Bondtech's CHT (Core Heating Technology) design, sold under brands like Mellow3D and Trianglelab on AliExpress. The CHT design splits filament into 3 strands through multiple bores to dramatically increase surface contact with the heater block walls. CNCKitchen testing consistently shows 25–35% higher volumetric flow compared to standard brass at 0.6mm and above. The M6 clones are effectively identical to the original Bondtech CHT at a fraction of the price and are the default nozzle recommendation for Voron builders wanting more speed without switching to hardened steel.

Pros:
Higher volumetric flow than standard Revo
Tool-free hot-swap retained
Good for speed printing with 0.6mm+
Cons:
Not available in 0.25mm (fine detail)
Pricier than standard Revo
Still not abrasive-safe
Name: Revo High Flow
Description: The Revo High Flow nozzle uses E3D's multi-bore high-flow geometry to increase volumetric throughput over the standard Revo nozzle. Designed for users who want faster print speeds without leaving the Revo ecosystem. Available in 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8mm. Retains the tool-free quick-swap mounting. Not to be confused with the ObXidian HF, which is also abrasive-safe.
Verdict Label: Revo speed upgrade for high-throughput printing

Pros:
Proprietary hardened alloy with 2.7x better thermal conductivity vs standard hardened steel
Low Gamma anti-adhesive coating rated to 380°C — non-PTFE, no temp ceiling for most materials
Limited Lifetime Warranty against abrasive wear
Multiple geometries: RepRap (V6), AP3X (belt/non-planar), Vase (large format), FIN (insulated)
Rockwell C63 hardness
100% Made in USA
Engraved orifice size on three sides
Cons:
Higher price than generic hardened steel options
Low Gamma coating degrades above 380°C (substrate itself rated to 500°C)
FIN geometry only compatible with Mako hotend currently
Name: GammaMaster
Description: The GammaMaster is Slice Engineering's flagship nozzle, made from a proprietary hardened alloy that achieves 2.7x the thermal conductivity of standard hardened steel — meaning no need to raise nozzle temperatures when printing abrasive filaments. Features their Low Gamma anti-adhesive surface coating (rated to 380°C) to prevent plastic buildup at the tip. Available in four geometries: RepRap (standard V6, M6 threading), AP3X (2mm longer tip for belt printers and non-planar printing), Vase (large-format vase mode), and FIN (insulated nozzle standard, Mako hotend only). Orifice sizes from 0.2mm to 1.8mm (plus 2.4mm Vase). Carries a Limited Lifetime Warranty against abrasive wear. Sold direct by Slice Engineering.

Pros:
Vanadium tool steel — excellent hardness and wear resistance for abrasive filaments
Better thermal conductivity than standard hardened steel
Currently on sale at $30.61 (from $43.74)
Cons:
Less community data and testing vs. more common hardened steel or SiC options
Limited ecosystem — primarily sold via Bondtech, harder to source through other vendors
Vanadium steel properties still being evaluated by community vs. alternatives
Name: Vanadium
Description: Bondtech's Vanadium Nozzle uses vanadium tool steel, a high-hardness alloy used in industrial cutting tools. Vanadium steel offers abrasion resistance comparable to hardened steel with potentially better thermal properties. Less common in the 3D printing nozzle market than hardened steel or bimetal alternatives. Sold directly by Bondtech. Currently listed on sale.

Pros:
Longer melt zone vs standard M6 — excellent for 0.6mm+ at speed
Standard Volcano M6 thread — widely compatible
Very affordable
Available in hardened steel and ruby tip variants
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe (brass)
Requires Volcano-length heater block — not interchangeable with standard M6 blocks
Minimum practical diameter higher than standard nozzles
Name: Volcano
Description: Standard Volcano-format brass nozzle from Trianglelab. The Volcano body is approximately 2× longer than a standard M6 nozzle, providing a larger melt zone for higher volumetric output — especially effective at 0.6mm+ diameters. Standard choice for Dragon HF, Rapido HF/UHF, and original E3D Volcano builds. Available in brass, hardened steel, and ruby tip variants from Trianglelab. Brass version is the common recommendation for high-speed printing with non-abrasive filaments.

Pros:
Silicon carbide is harder than hardened steel with significantly better thermal conductivity
No temperature penalty vs. brass when printing abrasive filaments
Available for multiple printer ecosystems: V6/Dragon/Rapido (M6), Prusa Nextruder, Creality K2, AD5X
Competitive pricing starting at $16
Cons:
SiC is harder than HS but not as inert as PCD or Ruby for the most extreme abrasives
Limited community data vs. more established materials like Ruby or HS
Variant lineup can be confusing — different SKUs per printer platform
Name: SiC
Description: Phaetus's silicon carbide (SiC) nozzle is their flagship abrasion-resistant product. Silicon carbide sits above hardened steel in hardness while offering meaningfully better thermal conductivity — eliminating the temperature increase usually required when switching from brass to an abrasive-safe nozzle. Compatible with Rapido, Dragon, and other Phaetus hotends via standard M6 threading. Also available in printer-specific variants for Prusa Nextruder, Creality K2, AD5X, and others. Available in standard and high-flow geometries.

Pros:
Bimetallic design (copper body / hardened steel insert) — better thermal conductivity than all-steel
Abrasive-safe at budget price
Standard M6 thread
Cons:
Product naming inconsistent across AliExpress listings and Trianglelab site — may be listed as TZ Bimetal or similar
Less community documentation than Mellow CHT variants
For abrasive speed printing, CHT Hardened Steel offers better flow
Name: ZS
Description: Trianglelab bimetallic abrasive-safe nozzle marketed under the 'ZS' designation on AliExpress. Features a copper alloy body (for thermal conductivity) with a hardened steel insert — a bimetallic design that better balances heat transfer and wear resistance than an all-steel nozzle. Fits standard M6 RepRap thread. Note: this product line has been sold under varying names (ZS, TZ Bimetal) across different generations and storefronts — the 'ZS' designation does not appear on Trianglelab's current website. For abrasive-safe speed printing on Voron/RatRig, the CHT Hardened Steel is more commonly recommended due to the flow rate advantage.

Pros:
Standard M6 thread — widest hotend compatibility in the hobby
Well-toleranced from Trianglelab
Very affordable
Direct replacement for any M6 hotend
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe
No special geometry — generic M6 nozzles from any vendor work equally well
For speed, upgrade to CHT variant
Name: Dragon Brass
Description: Standard M6 brass nozzle from Trianglelab, commonly purchased as the replacement nozzle for their Dragon hotend. Uses standard RepRap M6×1 thread — compatible with any M6 hotend (Dragon, Dragon HF, E3D V6, Revo-less Voron builds, etc.). No special internal geometry. For speed builds, replace with a CHT variant; for abrasive filaments, upgrade to hardened steel or E3D ObXidian. Listed here as the Dragon-compatible M6 reference entry.
Verdict Label: Standard nozzle for Dragon and V6-compatible hotends

Pros:
Full solid tungsten carbide body — not just a TC tip
CHT-style high-flow internal geometry
V6 and MK8 thread variants available
Extreme abrasion resistance for CF/GF/SiC filaments
Community-designed with strong Voron/high-speed printing following
Cons:
Only available in 0.5mm — no other diameters
Premium price for community-designed product
Sold exclusively via Fabreeko (US-centric availability)
Name: Bozzle V2 Tungsten Carbide
Description: Designed by Rentable Socks, a community member in the Voron and high-speed printing space. The Bozzle V2 is a full solid tungsten carbide nozzle — not a brass body with TC tip — making it the most abrasion-resistant nozzle option short of PCD. Features a CHT-inspired internal geometry for high volumetric flow. Sold exclusively through Fabreeko. Available in 0.5mm only in V6 (M6) and MK8 threading.

Pros:
Bimetal construction: copper inner core for thermal conductivity + hardened steel outer shell for abrasion resistance
CHT geometry (Core Heating Technology) — 3-strand filament split for high flow rates
Solves the core tradeoff of CHT nozzles: coated brass degrades with abrasives, this does not
Available in M6, MK8, and Volcano sizes
Cons:
Premium price at ~$50 — significantly more than CHT coated brass ($25) or standard hardened steel
Some community reports of delamination in extreme high-cycle abrasive use
Heavier than brass alternatives
Name: CHT BiMetal
Description: The Bondtech CHT BiMetal Nozzle (also called CHT Bimetal) is a bimetal construction nozzle combining a copper inner body (for thermal conductivity) with a hardened steel outer shell and CHT (Core Heating Technology) internal geometry. This addresses the fundamental problem with CHT coated brass nozzles: the coating wears under sustained abrasive filament use. The bimetal design maintains CHT high-flow performance with genuine abrasion resistance. Available in M6 (RepRap V6 thread), MK8, and Volcano sizes. Sold direct by Bondtech.

Pros:
Teflon/PTFE exterior sleeve prevents PETG and sticky filaments from adhering to nozzle tip
Significantly reduces stringing and blobbing on PETG
Available in Brass, Plated Copper, and Hardened Steel base materials
Budget-friendly at $8.49
Cons:
Hard 280°C max — PTFE coating degrades and off-gases above this temperature
Not suitable for high-temp materials (ASA, PC, PA)
Not abrasion resistant — PTFE exterior is soft
Name: PlastiGlide
Description: Fabreeko's PlastiGlide is a V6-style nozzle with a PTFE/Teflon exterior sleeve around the tip zone. The coating prevents PETG, sticky PLA, and similar materials from adhering to the outside of the nozzle, dramatically reducing blobbing, oozing, and stringing. Max temp is 280°C — the PTFE limits high-temperature use. Available in Brass, Plated Copper, and Hardened Steel core materials. V6 threading (M6 x 1.0), 0.4mm and 0.6mm orifice sizes.

Pros:
Phaetus's proprietary EndCoat™ DLC-inspired surface coating provides anti-adhesive properties
Lowest price entry into coated abrasive nozzles at ~$9
Available for multiple printer platforms
Cons:
EndCoat™ coating longevity under sustained abrasive use is less proven than uncoated HS or SiC
Limited community testing data vs. more established options
Coating may degrade with very aggressive filaments (high SiC or metal-fill)
Name: EndCoat
Description: Phaetus's EndCoat™ nozzle uses their proprietary diamond-like carbon (DLC) inspired coating applied to a hardened steel substrate. The coating reduces surface energy for anti-adhesion at the nozzle tip while maintaining the abrasion resistance of the hardened steel base. Entry-level coated nozzle option at ~$9. Available for Rapido/Dragon (M6), and multiple printer-specific platforms. Multiple variants in the Phaetus catalog (EndCoat K2 Series at $12.90, EndCoat Creality at $12.90, etc.).

Pros:
Tool-free hot-swap at temperature
Wide diameter range (0.15mm to 1.0mm)
No nozzle-block thread stripping risk
Accurate, machined brass for PLA/PETG/ABS
Cons:
Proprietary system — only works with Revo hotends
Not abrasive-safe (brass wears with CF/GF)
Premium price per nozzle vs generic M6
Name: Revo Brass
Description: E3D's RapidChange Revo nozzle attaches directly to the heater core rather than threading into a heater block. The tool-free hot-swap system lets you change diameters in seconds while the hotend is at temp — no wrenches, no stripped threads. The entry-level option in the Revo nozzle lineup, these standard brass nozzles cover PLA, PETG, ASA, and ABS with diameters spanning 0.15mm to 1.0mm. For abrasive filaments, step up to the Revo ObXidian or HTA variants.
Verdict Label: The easiest nozzle upgrade: hot-swap in seconds, no tools

Pros:
True PCD insert — not a coating, permanent abrasion resistance
Exceptional thermal conductivity vs. hardened steel
Made in USA by an industrial diamond tooling manufacturer
Multiple platform variants available (Bambu, Nextruder, Revo, K2, MK8)
Cons:
Very high price point — premium over all other abrasive-safe options
Overkill for occasional CF/GF use
Limited diameter selection vs. standard nozzle lines
Name: DiamondBack V6
Description: DiamondBack Nozzles is a brand of US Synthetic Corporation (Orem, Utah), a manufacturer of polycrystalline diamond (PCD) industrial cutting tools. Their 3D printer nozzles use a solid PCD insert — not a coating — providing virtually permanent wear resistance against abrasive filaments. E3D carries DiamondBack as an authorized distribution partner; DiamondBack also sells direct at diamondbacknozzles.com. The V6-compatible version fits standard E3D V6, Dragon, and Rapido hotends with M6 threading. Additional platform variants available for Bambu Lab, Prusa Nextruder, Revo, and Creality K2.
Verdict Label: Industrial-grade PCD tip — extreme wear resistance at extreme cost

Pros:
E3DLC diamond-like coating — significantly outperforms standard hardened steel
Reduces plastic adhesion and stringing at tip
Standard M6 thread — drop-in for any V6-compatible hotend
Available in fine sizes down to 0.25mm
Cons:
Premium price (~$32) vs clone hardened steel (~$3)
Max temp 300°C — not for ultra-high temp materials
Sometimes out of stock
Name: ObXidian V6
Description: E3D's ObXidian nozzles use an E3DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating that delivers exceptional wear resistance against abrasive filaments (CF, GF, metal fills). Community consensus puts ObXidian significantly ahead of standard hardened steel in wear life while maintaining better surface finish. The V6 model uses standard M6 thread and fits any V6-compatible hotend — Dragon, Rapido, Mosquito (with adapter), and others. Available in Revo-threaded variant as well.
Verdict Label: Best M6 abrasion-resistant nozzle for V6/Dragon/Rapido builds

Pros:
Standard M6 thread — drop-in for Rapido, Dragon, and any M6 hotend
Phaetus QC is generally solid
Available in hardened steel and ruby tip variants
Cons:
Not abrasive-safe (brass)
Rapido HF and UHF use Volcano-length nozzles, not standard M6 — confirm variant before ordering
No geometry advantages over other M6 nozzles
Name: Rapido Brass
Description: Standard M6 brass nozzle from Phaetus, sold as the replacement nozzle for their Rapido hotend series. The Rapido V1/V2 standard flow uses standard M6 length; the Rapido HF uses Volcano-length nozzles — confirm which Rapido variant you have before ordering. Standard M6 thread, no special bore geometry. For abrasive-safe printing on Rapido, CHT Hardened Steel or E3D ObXidian V6 (both standard M6) are the recommended upgrades.
Verdict Label: Standard nozzle for Rapido and Phaetus hotend ecosystem
